facility_roles.quote: ASACUSA aims to precisely measure a property of antihydrogen called the “hyperfine structure” and compare it to the well-known value for hydrogen.

intervals.note: Start is a lower bound: the CERN Courier of 17 August 2000 reports the AD "coming into action for physics" and supplying ATRAP, ATHENA and ASACUSA; the experiment's own first-data date is not stated in a source consulted. End: 31 August 2026 (LS3).
intervals.quote: This is the motivation behind CERN’s new AD, which supplies antiprotons to several experiments – ATRAP (son of TRAP at LEAR), ATHENA and ASACUSA.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 (no antiproton beam)
intervals.note: The Antimatter Factory (AD and ELENA) delivered its last beams on 31 August 2026 and "will progressively return to operation from 2028 onwards, with the different injectors and facilities restarting in stages" (CERN, 31 August 2026); no experiment-specific restart date is published, so the end is left open.
intervals.quote: CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent.

physics_goals.quote: The Atomic Spectroscopy And Collisions Using Slow Antiprotons (ASACUSA) experiment studies the fundamental symmetries between matter and antimatter by precision spectroscopy of atoms containing an antiproton
physics_goals.value: Study the fundamental symmetries between matter and antimatter by precision spectroscopy of atoms containing an antiproton, and study matter-antimatter collisions

summary.plain: A CERN experiment that compares matter and antimatter using atoms that contain an antiproton: antiprotonic helium and antihydrogen. It also studies what happens when antiprotons collide with ordinary atoms.
summary.technical: ASACUSA (Atomic Spectroscopy And Collisions Using Slow Antiprotons, AD-1): laser spectroscopy of antiprotonic helium, a cusp-trap antihydrogen beam for ground-state hyperfine spectroscopy in flight, and antiproton-atom collision studies, using the AD radio-frequency decelerator. At the AD since 2000; paused for LS3.
